- [2023/05/26] Wallabies in the wild generally have a lifespan of 7-9 years, while those in captivity can live up to 15-20 years or more with proper care.
- [2023/05/26] A balanced diet for wallabies should include fresh fruits, vegetables, hay, and possibly commercial diets formulated for them.
- [2023/05/26] Wallabies require grass hay, fresh leafy greens (like kale, spinach, and lettuce), fruits (such as apples, bananas, and berries), and vegetables (like carrots, beets, sweet potatoes, and squash) in their diet.
- [2023/05/26] Wallabies are primarily herbivorous and do not typically eat insects or meat, though some keepers may add small amounts of cooked, lean meat or insects for protein.
- [2023/05/26] Fruits not recommended for wallabies include citrus fruits, avocado, grapes or raisins, rhubarb, and unripe fruits due to potential toxicity or digestive issues.
- [2023/05/26] Wallabies need a large, secure outdoor enclosure, socialization, regular veterinary care, proper shelter, and a secure environment.
- [2023/05/26] Owning a wallaby requires checking legal restrictions, providing extensive space, meeting dietary needs, managing expenses, ensuring socialization, and committing to their long lifespan of up to 15-20 years in captivity.
